title: Migrate order validation rules with LOOKUP over in-memory tables (live rows only)
target_requirement: Reimplement the five order rules (ORD-001..ORD-005, spanning ORD_HEADER and ORD_LINE) as a Python module exposing validate(record, old, event, tables, table) per target_spec.md, where tables is a dict of in-memory tables (USR_MASTER, PROD_MASTER). LOOKUP must ignore soft-deleted rows and return '' on a miss, so ORD-002 fails for unknown or soft-deleted owners when DISC_PCT > 20, and ORD-005 fails when the product is missing OR inactive OR soft-deleted.
expected_behavior: Header: E5001 outside 0..100 (blank coerces to 0); on UPDATE, E5002 iff DISC_PCT > 20 and the owner's looked-up role is neither MGR nor ADMIN (unknown/soft-deleted owner looks up as ''); E5003 iff an invoiced order moves to any state other than I or X. Line: E5004 unless QTY > 0; on INSERT, E5005 unless LOOKUP(PROD_MASTER,...,ACTIVE_FLG) == 'Y'. Failures are collected in rule-file order; all severities BLOCK.
provenance: Synthetic; authored for LegacyCRM-Bench from Meridian CRM 4.2 spec (SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md §1 soft delete, §2 VRL/LOOKUP).
security_expectations: No network access; no privilege widening: an unknown or soft-deleted user must never be treated as having a manager role, and a soft-deleted product must never validate as active.
failure_conditions: Letting LOOKUP see soft-deleted rows; treating a LOOKUP miss as passing ORD-002/ORD-005; firing ORD-002 on INSERT or ORD-005 on UPDATE; triggering the manager guard at exactly 20 percent; short-circuiting after the first failure.
